descriptionChirho: Qal participle used substantively to denote the agent who destroys, despoils, or plunders, whether singular or plural, with or without the article.
Active Qal forms expressing the verbal action of destroying, plundering, or laying waste, including finite verbs, verbal participles, imperatives, and infinitives.
Piel stem forms expressing intensive or deliberate destruction, assault, or ruination beyond the basic Qal sense.
Pual passive perfects indicating the state of having been devastated, destroyed, or ruined, used of cities, lands, and peoples.
Qal passive participles, Qal passive imperfects, and Nifal forms expressing the state or process of being destroyed or devastated.
Qal infinitive absolute used adverbially to intensify a following finite verb, conveying the totality or completeness of the destruction.
